items.note: AA9 is not in the service registry and the CSV carries exactly one physical vessel — WAN HAI 712. It prints two voyage rows, E001 and E002; E001 is a truncated duplicate of the same sailing (identical dates from Cai Mep onward, no Port Klang call, no US calls), so n equals 1 in-window sailing, not 2. Single-vessel, single-voyage, no second string behind it — an extra loader, not a service. Ningbo ETD 03 Sep and Qingdao ETD 06 Sep are both in window; the Port Klang leg on 23 Aug falls in W34, outside it. Proforma benchmark is cross-carrier (Evergreen NUE on Ningbo-New York, 34d for the EVER LIVELY sailing of 02 Sep) because no like-for-like Wan Hai AA7 Ningbo-New York transit was captured this run — treat the +4d delta as indicative, not exact. TEU carried forward from the prior run; rotation matched the stored copy byte-for-byte, so it was not re-scraped from Atlas.

history.note: RETIRED TO HISTORY 27 Aug 2026 after a second consecutive run with no in-window sailing. This run Maersk's own routings-queries API was replayed successfully for Yantian-Houston across the full W35-W42 window and returned 9 direct sailings, every one of them isRoutingAdhoc false, with no MAERSK MONTANA among them (GSL GRANIA, MAERSK SANA, TACOMA MAERSK, SAN FERNANDO, TEMA MAERSK, MAERSK LAVRAS, MAERSK SAIGON, MAERSK SANTANA, MAERSK ATHABASCA). Hapag's Gemini view of KRPUS-USHOU independently returned 6 US3 sailings with no MONTANA either. Two independent negatives on the exact lane, so this is retired rather than carried. It was never verified against a scraped schedule in the first place — it entered the file as a carry-forward from market.json and should not have been published without a rotation.

alerts.msg: No in-window sailing for two consecutive runs. Moved to history, not deleted. Retirement is backed by two independent negatives this run: Maersk routings-queries for Yantian-Houston over the full window returned 9 direct sailings, all isRoutingAdhoc false, none of them MONTANA; Hapag's Busan-Houston view returned 6 US3 sailings, also none. It had never been schedule-verified.

Evergreen Yantian-Houston returned service code AUG with n=3 in-window sailings (ONE HUMEN 101E ETD 06 Sep, CONTI CORTESIA 014E ETD 11 Sep, MOL CREATION 103E ETD 28 Aug). AUG is not in the registry and not on the deny-list. n>=3 means NEW SERVICE, not an extra loader, so nothing was published for it. Registry NOT updated this run — per the rule it needs a second run to confirm before promotion. If the next run also returns n>=3, add AUG to Ocean Alliance.

Lanes not covered this run: all CMA CGM lanes (not attempted — the routing-finder POST recipe lives in the liner-tracker-market-refresh task and was not available to this run, and the DataDome quota is shared with that task on the same IP); all MSC and ZIM lanes; all ONE lanes; Hapag Cai Mep (VNCMT and VNTOT both returned HTTP 400 — the correct Hapag LOCODE for Cai Mep is unresolved); Maersk Yantian-New York, Yantian-Savannah and all Shanghai/Ningbo/Busan lanes; Evergreen Busan, Xiamen, Qingdao, Singapore, Port Klang and Kaohsiung origins; Evergreen Shanghai/Ningbo/Cai Mep to Savannah and Houston.

Not attempted. The routing-finder POST recipe is defined by reference to the liner-tracker-market-refresh task and was not reproducible from this run's context. No DataDome quota was consumed, which also means none was taken from the market-refresh task.

ShipmentLink caps durationWeek at 28 days, so a single pass sees 4 weeks, not the full 8-week window. A second pass was run with departureDay +28 (Yantian-New York from 24 Sep) and returned only 3 rows — SAX 28 Sep, AUE 26 Sep, CBX 26 Sep — which means Evergreen has simply not published beyond roughly 28 Sep on this lane yet. Effective Evergreen visibility this run is W35-W40, not W35-W42.

All three regression fixtures passed. Evergreen Yantian-New York 4wk: SAX 4, CBX 3, AUE 4, OGEC 1 — OGEC flagged, nothing else. Evergreen Shanghai-New York 4wk: SAX 4, NUE 4, NUE2 1, CBX 3, OGEC 1 — OGEC flagged, nothing else. Hapag Yantian-New York 8wk: AA7 5 with isGemini false, US4 6 with isGemini true — nothing flagged, so the registry lookup and the isGemini trap are both still behaving.

Maersk's routings-queries response carries an explicit isRoutingAdhoc boolean on every routing. That makes Maersk the second portal after Evergreen that labels ad-hoc sailings directly rather than requiring frequency inference. Worth wiring into PART 2 as a `label` trigger. Also confirmed this run: Hapag's schedule API tolerated 14 sequential fetches from one renderer, so the documented 'roughly one fetch per navigation' limit is more pessimistic than observed.
